title: Canary Token Check
description: Starter pseudocode for the canary token task: a function that checks outbound text for a secret canary value, logs the detection, and blocks the send.

steps.description: This is the starter pseudocode for the canary token task. The page says a canary is a value the agent reads but should never send, and this function runs before any tool sends data outside the agent's process. It imports `logging` and `datetime` and defines the canary constant.

`check_for_canary` takes the outbound text and the canary value, which defaults to the constant. The docstring says it returns `True` when the send is safe and `False` when the canary is found, and that you call it before every outbound tool action.

When the canary appears in the outbound text, the function logs two critical lines: the detection time from `datetime` and the first 500 characters of the outbound text. The page says the log carries a timestamp and context for forensic investigation.

The comment lists the response: revoke agent credentials, halt execution, and alert on-call. `trigger_incident_response()` is left for you to implement. The function then returns `False` to block the outbound action, and returns `True` when no canary is found.
